content: 1. The study titled Ribavirin Plus R for the Treatment of HCV Genotype 2 Infection presents real-world clinical practice results from the HCV-TARGET study, published in Gut in 2016. 2. Wilder JM, Shiffman M, Sulkowski M, Yang J, Pang P, McHutchison J, Muir A, and Reddy KR conducted a retrospective analysis of phase 3 data to evaluate the safety and efficacy of ledipasvir-sofosbuvir in Black patients with hepatitis C virus (HCV) infection, published in Hepatology in 2016. 3. Subramanian G, Pang P, McHutchison J, and Kottilil S reported successful retreatment of chronic HCV genotype 1 infection using ledipasvir and sofosbuvir after initial short-course therapy with direct-acting antiviral regimens, as published in Clinical Infectious Diseases in 2016. 4. Wyles D, Brau N, Kottilil S, et al. conducted an open-label phase 3 study on the use of sofosbuvir and velpatasvir for treating HCV in patients co-infected with HIV-1, published in Clinical Infectious Diseases in 2017. 5. Wyles D, Brau N, Naggie S, et al. compared the efficacy and safety of the single-tablet regimen of sofosbuvir/velpatasvir in HCV mono-infected and HIV/HCV co-infected patients, based on phase 3 clinical trials, presented at the Journal of the International AIDS Society Conference in 2016. 6. Wyle S, Ruane P, Sulkowski M, et al. evaluated daclatasvir in combination with sofosbuvir for HIV/HCV co-infection in the ALLY-2 study, published in Top Antiviral Medicine in 2015. 7. Wyles DL, Sulkowski M, Morgan T, Sherman K, Gathe J, Overton E, Yin P, and the ALLY investigators studied the combination of daclatasvir and sofosbuvir for HCV in patients co-infected with HIV-1, published in the New England Journal of Medicine in 2015. 8. Sulkowski M, Luetkemeyer A, Morgan T, Sherman K, and Ackerman P investigated the use of daclatasvir and sofosbuvir for treating HCV genotypes 1-4 in HIV-HCV co-infected patients in the ALLY-2 study, published in the Journal of Hepatology in 2015. 9. Yakoot M, Abdo AM, Abdel-Rehim S, and Helmy S conducted a randomized, open-label, non-inferiority trial comparing a response-tailored protocol versus a fixed 12-week course of dual sofosbuvir/daclatasvir treatment in Egyptian patients with chronic HCV genotype 4 infection, published in EBioMedicine in 2017. 10. Yao Y, Yue M, Wang J, et al. performed a comprehensive efficacy and safety analysis of grazoprevir and elbasvir in patients with genotype 1 HCV infection, published in Canadian Journal of Gastroenterology and Hepatology in 2017. 11. Yoshimi S, Imamura M, Murakami E, et al. studied the long-term persistence of NS5A inhibitor-resistant HCV in patients who failed daclatasvir and asunaprevir therapy, published in the Journal of Medical Virology in 2015. 12. Younossi Z, Stepanova M, Han KH, et al. reported very high efficacy and improved health-related quality of life (HRQL) in Asian patients with HCV genotype 1 treated with ledipasvir and sofosbuvir, published in the Journal of Gastroenterology and Hepatology in 2016. 13. Younossi ZM, Park H, Gordon SC, et al. analyzed real-world outcomes of ledipasvir/sofosbuvir in treatment-naïve patients with HCV, published in the American Journal of Managed Care in 2016. 14. Younossi ZM, Stepanova M, Charlton M, et al. explored patient-reported outcomes with sofosbuvir and velpatasvir, with or without ribavirin, in HCV-related decompensated cirrhosis, based on the ASTRAL-4 phase 3 trial, published in The Lancet Gastroenterology and Hepatology in 2016. 15. Younossi ZM, Stepanova M, Feld J, et al. demonstrated that sofosbuvir/velpatasvir improves patient-reported outcomes in HCV patients, as shown in the ASTRAL-1 placebo-controlled trial, published in the Journal of Hepatology in 2016. 16. Younossi ZM, Stepanova M, Omata M, Mizokami M, Walters M, and Hunt S evaluated the quality of life of Japanese patients with chronic HCV treated with ledipasvir and sofosbuvir, published in Medicine in 2016. 17. Younossi ZM, Stepanova M, Sulkowski M, et al. reported that a ribavirin-free regimen with sofosbuvir and velpatasvir is associated with high efficacy and improved patient-reported outcomes in patients with genotypes 2 and 3 chronic HCV, based on the ASTRAL-2 and -3 clinical trials, published in Clinical Infectious Diseases in 2016. 18. Younossi ZM, Stepanova M, Sulkowski M, Wyles D, Kottilil S, and Hunt S analyzed patient-reported outcomes in HCV and HIV co-infected patients treated with sofosbuvir and velpatasvir in the ASTRAL-5 study, published in Liver International in 2017. 19. Kowdley K, Hunt S, and Marcellin P demonstrated improvements in health-related quality of life and work productivity in chronic HCV patients with early and advanced fibrosis treated with ledipasvir and sofosbuvir, published in the Journal of Hepatology in 2015. 20. Hunt SL studied the impact of sofosbuvir and ribavirin on patient-reported outcomes in HCV and HIV co-infected patients, published in the Journal of Infectious Diseases in 2015. 21. Kowdley K and Hunt SL reported that treatment with ledipasvir and sofosbuvir improves patient-reported outcomes, based on results from the ION-1, -2, and -3 clinical trials, published in Hepatology in 2015. 22. Hunt S highlighted the improvement in patient-reported outcomes in HCV and HIV co-infected patients treated with sofosbuvir and ledipasvir, published in the Journal of Viral Hepatitis in 2016. 23. Bronowicki J, Carrieri M, and Bourliere M evaluated the impact of ledipasvir/sofosbuvir on patient-reported outcomes in cirrhotic patients with chronic HCV in the SIRIUS study, published in Liver International in 2016. 24. Bronowicki J and Bourliere M further analyzed the effect of ledipasvir/sofosbuvir on health-related quality of life and patient-reported outcomes in cirrhotic patients with chronic HCV, published in the Journal of Hepatology in 2015. 25. Hunt S assessed health utilities using SF-6D scores in Japanese patients with chronic HCV treated with sofosbuvir-based regimens in clinical trials, published in Health and Quality of Life Outcomes in 2017. 26. Zeng QL, Xu GH, Zhang JY, et al. conducted a real-life observational study on the use of generic ledipasvir-sofosbuvir in patients with chronic HCV, published in the Journal of Hepatology in 2017. 27. Zeuzem S, Dusheiko GM, Salupere R, et al. studied the efficacy of sofosbuvir and ribavirin in HCV genotypes 2 and 3, published in the New England Journal of Medicine in 2014. 28. Zeuzem S, Flamm SL, Tong MJ, et al. conducted a randomized, controlled phase 3 trial comparing sofosbuvir/velpatasvir/voxilaprevir and sofosbuvir/velpatasvir for 12 weeks in direct-acting antiviral-experienced patients with genotype 1-6 HCV infection, presented at the 67th Annual Meeting of the American Association for the Study of Liver Diseases in 2016. 29. Zeuzem S, Ghalib R, Reddy KR, et al. presented final SVR24 data from the phase 3 C-EDGE treatment-naïve study of elbasvir/grazoprevir in patients with chronic HCV genotype 1, 4, or 6 infection, published in the Journal of Hepatology in 2016. 30. Zeuzem S, Ghalib R, Reddy KR, et al. evaluated the 12-week oral regimen of grazoprevir/elbasvir in treatment-naïve patients with chronic HCV genotype 1, 4, or 6 infection, published in the Journal of Hepatology in 2015. 31. Zeuzem S, Ghalib R, Reddy KR, et al. studied the combination therapy of grazoprevir-elbasvir in treatment-naïve cirrhotic and non-cirrhotic patients with chronic HCV genotype 1, 4, or 6 infection, published in the Annals of Internal Medicine in 2015. 32. Zeuzem SD, Hyland R, Brainard D, Symonds W, McHutchison J, Reesink H, and Esteban R reported that early viral kinetics do not predict treatment outcomes with sofosbuvir and ribavirin for 12 or 24 weeks in HCV genotype 2/3 patients in the VALENCE trial, published in the Journal of Hepatology. 33. Zhdanov K, Orlova-Morozova EA, Morozov V, et al. evaluated ledipasvir/sofosbuvir in treatment-naïve patients with chronic HCV infection and HIV/HCV co-infection, as well as in sofosbuvir-experienced patients, presented at the 26th Annual Conference of the Asian Pacific Association for the Study of the Liver in 2017.
